newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-TOMS WINS QUAD CITY CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-TOMS WINS QUAD CITY CLASSIC.

text.p: David Toms won for the first time in his eight-year PGA career, firing a final-round five-under-par 65 for a three-shot victory in the $1.35 million PGA Quad City Classic Sunday.

Toms, who made his PGA Tour debut in 1991, began the day tied with Brad Fabel. At various times, he shared the lead with Robert Gamez, Bruce Fleisher and Jimmy Johnston, who fired an eight-under 62, one shy of Mike Smith's 1987 course record.

Toms grabbed the lead for good midway through his round, just before a 90-minute lightning delay. He finished at 15-under 265, three strokes in front of Johnston, Gamez and Brandel Chamblee, earning the $243,000 first prize.
"It hasn't hit me yet," said the 30-year-old Toms. "It's a great day in my life. I'm proud of myself."

A veteran of qualifying school and the Nike Tour, Toms earned an automatic two-year exemption in his 151st career PGA event. He became the third first-time winner on Tour this year and the 16th in the last two years.

"I have waited a long time for this," said Toms, whose previous best finish was third at the 1992 Northern Telecom Open. "A couple of wins on the Nike Tour certainly helped me to reach this point. It's nice to get over the hump. It was finally my time."

Johnston, who began the day six shots off the lead, finished at 12-under 268 with Gamez and Chamblee, both of whom shot 67s. Fabel carded a one-under 69 and tied for fifth at 269 with Frank Lickliter, who shot a 68.

With most of the PGA Tour's top players already overseas for the British Open, players such as Toms got a tremendous opportunity to win a PGA Tour event. Those remaining stateside will get a similar chance at next week's Deposit Guaranty Classic.
"Anytime you have a PGA Tour event, you have a quality field," Toms said. "So I know I beat some good players this week."

Toms drained a seven-foot birdie putt at the par-4 second hole, then overcame a bogey at the fourth with birdies at the sixth and ninth holes. He birdied the par-5 10th before lightning chased players off the course.
"At the rain delay, I was nervous," Toms admitted. "Then we went in and I ate and got in a corner. Then I came out relaxed."

With Johnston in the clubhouse, Toms sank a 20-foot birdie at the par-4 11th to open his lead to two shots. At 13, he missed a four-foot par putt that allowed Gamez to pull within a shot, but he rebounded nicely and took control for good.
At the par-4 14th, Toms sank a 12-foot birdie putt. At 15, his tee shot found the rough, but he blasted out to 30 feet and made the putt for another birdie and a three-stroke lead.
"I had chances in the past and I either didn't play well or somebody else beat me," he said. "Today is the best I ever played on Sunday with a chance to win. I overcame a hurdle today."
